title: Cap. VI Arg. 10: comparative election and rejection — an inscrutable abyss
latin: In comparativa electione et rejectione hominum est abyssus quaedam inscrutabilis, et arcanum nulla humana curiositate pulsandum. Nam si ad rationis humanae calculos revocaretur, injustitiae speciem prae se ferret, quod ex duobus prorsus aequalibus unus gratioso beneplacito Dei ad vitam destinatur, alter relinquitur.
pass_a: In the comparative election and rejection of men there is a certain inscrutable abyss, and a secret to be struck by no human curiosity. For if it were recalled to the calculations of human reason, it would wear the appearance of injustice, that from two altogether equal one is destined to life by the gracious good pleasure of God, the other is left.
pass_b: In comparative election and rejection of men there is an inscrutable abyss — a secret no human curiosity may pry into. Brought back to the sums of human reason, it would look like injustice: of two wholly equal, one is destined to life by God's gracious good pleasure, the other left.

title: Cap. VI Arg. 10: Rom. 9 — Jacob and Esau; objection of injustice referred to Rom. 11:33-34
latin: Ostentum est hoc ab Apostolo, Rom. ix. ubi gratuita Jacobi electione et Esavi praeteritione declarata, statim amolitur illam objectionem, quam humana ratio suggerit, nimirum, Posito tali beneplacito, secundum quod nondum natis fratribus, priusquam nihil fecissent boni vel mali, unus diligatur, alter odio habeatur, injustitiam quandam esse apud Deum, vers. 14. Quam objectionem non solvendo solvit, dum ad inscrutabilem altitudinem sapientiae ac judicii Divini referendam docet, Rom. xi. vers. 33. 34.
pass_a: This is shown by the Apostle, Rom. 9, where the gratuitous election of Jacob and the passing by of Esau being declared, he at once removes that objection which human reason suggests, namely, Such a good pleasure being posited, according to which of brothers not yet born, before they had done anything good or evil, one is loved, the other hated, that there is a certain injustice with God, verse 14. Which objection he solves by not solving, while he teaches that it is to be referred to the inscrutable height of Divine wisdom and judgment, Rom. 11:33-34.
pass_b: Paul shows it in Rom. 9: after stating Jacob's gratuitous election and Esau's being passed by, he at once thrusts off the objection human reason prompts — that if by such good pleasure one unborn brother is loved and the other hated before either did good or evil, there is injustice with God (v. 14). He solves it by not solving it: he sends it up to the inscrutable height of divine wisdom and judgment (Rom. 11:33-34).

lemmas.gloss: inscrutable height of wisdom and judgment

title: Cap. VI Arg. 10: foresight election empties the secret — Peter and Judas already explained
latin: Omnes Orthodoxi in hoc praedestinationis et praeteritionis negotio tale arcanum agnoverunt, et Praedestinationem ex praevisis actibus humanis eo argumento rejiciunt, quod tale arcanum excludat. Nam si Petrus praedestinatus fuerit quia praevidebatur a Deo ut crediturus, et in fide perseveraturus, Judas praeteritus fuerit quia praevidebatur ut in sua infidelitate moriturus, ratio praedestinandi et non praedestinandi jam in propatulo erit, nec quicquam arcani in se continebit.
pass_a: All the Orthodox in this business of predestination and passing by have acknowledged such a secret, and reject Predestination from foresighted human acts by this argument, that it excludes such a secret. For if Peter was predestinated because he was foreseen by God as about to believe, and about to persevere in faith, Judas was passed by because he was foreseen as about to die in his unbelief, the reason of predestinating and of not predestinating will already be in the open, and will contain nothing of secret in itself.
pass_b: All the Orthodox in this business of predestination and passing by have owned that secret — and reject predestination from foresighted human acts just because that empties the secret. If Peter was predestined because God foresaw he would believe and persevere, and Judas passed by because foresaw he would die in unbelief, the reason for predestining and not predestining is already out in the open, with nothing secret left.

lemmas.gloss: if foresight explains both, nothing remains hidden

title: Cap. VI Arg. 10: Augustine and Prosper — depth of grace not opened by free choice
latin: At longe aliter sanctus Augustinus Contr. 2. Epistol. Pelag. lib. 4. cap. 6: Quare istos oves facit, et istos non facit, apud quem non est acceptio personarum, ipsa est quaestio quae pertinet ad illam altitudinem, etc. Et Prosper, De vocat. gent. lib. 1. cap. 23: Frustra profunditatem inscrutabilis gratiae per liberum arbitrium conantur aperire, qui causam electionis in eorum constituunt meritis qui eliguntur. Et cap. ultimo: Profunditas illius quaestionis, quam secundum admirationem Apostoli impervestigabilem confitemur, per liberi arbitrii velle et nolle non solvitur.
pass_a: But far otherwise holy Augustine, Against Two Letters of the Pelagians, book 4, chapter 6: Why he makes these sheep, and those not, with whom there is no respect of persons, that itself is the question which pertains to that height, etc. And Prosper, On the Calling of the Gentiles, book 1, chapter 23: In vain do they try to open the depth of inscrutable grace through free choice, who set the cause of election in the merits of those who are elected. And in the last chapter: The depth of that question, which according to the Apostle's admiration we confess unsearchable, is not solved by the willing and not-willing of free choice.
pass_b: Far otherwise Augustine (Against Two Letters of the Pelagians 4.6): why he makes these sheep and not those — with whom there is no respect of persons — that very question belongs to that height. And Prosper (On the Calling of the Gentiles 1.23): in vain they try to open the depth of inscrutable grace by free choice, who plant election's cause in the merits of the elect. And in the last chapter: that question's depth, which with the Apostle's wonder we confess unsearchable, is not solved by free choice's willing and refusing.

lemmas.gloss: why these sheep and not those
depth not solved by free choice

title: Cap. VI Arg. 10 close: same against Arminians — no easy ratio of elect and rejected
latin: Quod itaque a Catholicis olim contra Semipelagianos recte dictum fuit, idem nos in Arminianos electionem ex praevisione fidei et finalis perseverantiae statuentes torquemus: Haec si ita sint, comprehensa sunt a vobis inscrutabilia judicia Dei, etc. Nos autem incomprehensibilia credentes et demonstrantes judicia Dei, ex una massa perditionis alios salvari dicimus bonitate et gratia Dei, alios justo et occulto judicio derelinqui, Petr. Diac. De Incarn. cap. 7. Est ergo rejicienda illorum omnium sententia, qui tam facili compendio rationem reddunt electorum et rejectorum, quam neque orthodoxi Patres, nec ipse Apostolus in tertium caelum raptus reddere potuit.
pass_a: What therefore was rightly said of old by the Catholics against the Semi-Pelagians, the same we twist upon the Arminians who establish election from foresight of faith and final perseverance: If these things are so, the inscrutable judgments of God have been comprehended by you, etc. But we, believing and demonstrating the incomprehensible judgments of God, say that from one mass of perdition some are saved by the goodness and grace of God, others are left by just and hidden judgment, Peter the Deacon, On the Incarnation, chapter 7. Therefore the opinion of all those is to be rejected, who by so easy a short cut render the reason of the elect and the rejected, which neither the orthodox Fathers, nor the Apostle himself caught up into the third heaven, was able to render.
pass_b: What Catholics once rightly said against the Semi-Pelagians, we turn on Arminians who ground election in foresight of faith and final perseverance: if so, you have comprehended God's inscrutable judgments. We, believing and showing those judgments incomprehensible, say that from one mass of perdition some are saved by God's goodness and grace, others left by just and hidden judgment (Peter the Deacon, On the Incarnation 7). Reject, then, all who give so easy a short-cut reason of elect and rejected — a reason neither the orthodox Fathers nor the Apostle himself, caught up to the third heaven, could give.

lemmas.gloss: even Paul rapt to the third heaven could not give the ratio
